coachingReport.introduction: Hi there! I'm Nora. I absolutely loved reading through this transcript. The imaginative connection you share with Lucas is so beautiful to witness. You are doing an incredible job engaging with him!

topMoment.title: Entering His World
topMoment.explanation: By enthusiastically joining his pretend play and following his lead, you are making a massive deposit into Lucas's emotional bank account. This kind of child-led play acts as a powerful 'emotional massage,' soothing his nervous system and building the deep trust needed to navigate harder moments like screen-time transitions.

nextGrowthFocus.title: Scaffolding Screen-Time Transitions
nextGrowthFocus.explanation: You mentioned in your notes that screen time often ends without a warning, leading to big feelings and tantrums. For a 5-year-old with ADHD, the brain hyper-focuses on the screen. A sudden stop feels like a shock to his nervous system because task-switching is developmentally challenging for him.

strategies.name: Countdown Warnings
strategies.description: Provide clear, predictable time markers before the screen turns off so his brain can prepare for the shift.

strategies.name: Bridge to Offline Play
strategies.description: Use his love for pretend play (like KidStop) as the immediate next activity to make the transition appealing.

nextGrowthFocus.exampleQuote: Lucas, we have 5 more minutes of screen time, and then it's time to play KidStop!
nextGrowthFocus.rationale: Predictability reduces anxiety. It gives his ADHD brain the runway it needs to shift gears safely, significantly reducing the intensity of the tantrums and helping him feel secure.

whatWeLearned.title: What We Learned About Lucas
whatWeLearned.description: Lucas has a rich imagination and thrives when you participate in his world. We can use this to our advantage! By offering a few minutes of 'emotional massage' through pretend play right after screens, we create a highly rewarding bridge that makes turning off the device much easier for him.

myPlan.whyItWorks: Lucas's ADHD brain struggles with abrupt task-switching. Predictable warnings give his nervous system the necessary time to prepare for the end of screen time without triggering a tantrum.
protocolSteps: Give a calm 5-minute warning before screen time ends.
Give a 2-minute warning, gently touching his shoulder to ensure he hears you.
At zero, confidently state screen time is over and bridge to pretend play.

crisisTool.title: Managing Big Feelings Tantrums
crisisTool.action: Sit within arm's reach, take deep breaths, and wait for the storm to pass without negotiating.
crisisTool.script: You are so mad screen time is over. It is hard to stop. I am right here with you.
